postings.title: Business Controller
postings.description: About this positionA division that doubles in size within a few years leaves little to hold onto in terms of existing systems — but gives you plenty of room to build them yourself. That's exactly where this role puts you. As Division Business Controller at EMO (Electromagnetics & Military Operations), you're not the executor of a control cycle that has run the same way for years; you help shape what financial steering looks like in a division that is constantly growing and developing innovative solutions in the field of electromagnetic technology and military operations.You carry P&L responsibility for the entire division and serve as the primary financial sounding board for the division director. You also provide functional leadership to the project controllers — shaping how they do their work, without being their formal line manager. For those who prefer building over maintaining, and who don't get thrown off by pace, this is a role you can really sink your teeth into. You are part of a team of three other division controllers and eight project controllers, and you report to the unit controller.Security is not a given. Sometimes you have to fight for peace. There is always a frontline somewhere where history is being written. The impact of rising global tensions — in particular the ongoing conflict over Ukraine — on our armed forces is significant. The knowledge and technology needs of our founding partner Defence are evolving faster and shifting; the pace is increasing and research and development budgets are growing rapidly. In line with this, attention to our national (domestic) security is also intensifying — for example in the fight against the hardening drugs-related crime in our own country. This is where knowledge and technology make the difference, and that is what we translate into our mission.What will be your role?You're close to the action: the division director and management team rely on your insight to stay on course while the organisation around them evolves. In concrete terms:You coordinate the planning and control cycle and ensure clear, reliable management reporting.You advise — proactively and reactively — on financial steering, business cases and investment decisions, including toward research managers. You are a standard attendee at the division's MT meetings.You assess calculations and risks on large, complex projects and advise on whether to accept them.You provide functional guidance to the project controllers: monitoring quality and consistency, and supporting their professional development.You have the space to build what doesn't yet exist: processes, reports and ways of working that scale with the pace of the division.What we expect from youYou are an experienced (business) controller with a sharp eye for figures and for the organisation around them. Growth and pace don't feel like threats to you — they're your playing field. You maintain overview, prioritise decisively and know exactly what you stand for even when the pressure is on. And plenty of opportunities as, at TNO, you are in charge of shaping your career. postings.title: Internship | Cloud Resource Models for Virtual Core
postings.description: About this positionThe growing deployment of latency-sensitive applications such as autonomous systems, industrial automation, augmented reality, and private 5G networks is driving a strong demand for edge computing infrastructures capable of hosting cloud-native network functions close to end users. In this context, resource models that estimate the performance of Cloud-native Network Functions (CNFs) deployed on Commercial-Of-The-Shelf (COTS) hardware under varying workloads, resource allocations, and deployment conditions are becoming increasingly important. These models enable operators to forecast key performance indicators such as throughput, latency, packet loss, and resource utilization before deployment or scaling actions occur.This internship focuses on the research and development of a model of compute infrastructure whose purpose is to facilitate CNF deployment optimization. You will work with our team on the analysis of CNF resource use and contribute to solutions that help advance the models used for network optimization. You will be part of an environment where curiosity is encouraged, ideas are welcome, and you have the space to develop your expertise.What will be your role?The performance of user plane CNFs deployed on COTS computing platforms is influenced by numerous interacting factors, including compute resources, virtualization layers, memory behavior, I/O subsystems, deployment configurations, and packet processing mechanisms. The relationship(s) between these factors and their impact on packet forwarding is very complex, making the development of reliable and scalable performance models challenging.During the internship, you will address this challenge with an empirical approach. You will develop and deploy a representative experimental environment in our lab which can generate reliable performance measurements. The experiment runs will target a device under test (DUT) which is a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) cloud compute host running containerized XDP-based User Plane Functions (UPFs). The emphasis with the runs is on understanding the bottlenecks and system features of both traffic generation and forwarding via the DUT. You will then analyze the experiment results and choose the most important factors and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), which will be included in the development of a resource model that predict the performance of CNFs deployed on the COTS machine.The overall goal is to combine system operation, development, benchmarking and modelling knowledge to enable more representative models of infrastructures running the cloud-native user-plane of next generation networks.What we expect from youWe are looking for a master student with a background in Computer Science and/or Engineering who has an interest in Computer Networking. You have basic skills in operating systems, coding in C/C++ and Python, or the motivation to quickly develop them. It helps if you have knowledge of Linux networking, eXpress Data Path, packet generation and queueing theory, but we are happy to support you in developing your knowledge in these areas. What matters most is that you are curious, proactive, and enjoy working together on the performance of networking workloads in virtual environments. This work can be scoped as an internship or as a MSc thesis project, depending on your need.What you'll get in returnAn internship at TNO means working in an environment where substance and impact are central. You will become part of a knowledge organisation where research and practice come together, and where experts collaborate on solutions to current societal and technological challenges.Your internship is a period in which you can discover what suits you, where your strengths lie and what you would like to learn next. postings.title: Internship | Design of phased array in E-Band for future SATCOM applications
postings.description: About this positionFuture satellite communication systems need to transmit increasingly large amounts of data. Moving towards higher frequencies, such as E-band, can provide the required capacity, but it also creates new challenges for antenna design. The antennas must generate highly directional beams, scan over a wide angular range and operate efficiently despite the losses associated with these frequencies.This internship focuses on the development of a novel antenna array for future E-band satellite communication systems. You will work with our antenna research team to investigate different array technologies and identify promising solutions for efficient, wide-angle beam scanning. Your work will contribute to the development of advanced antenna systems that can support future high-capacity satellite links.You will be part of a collaborative research environment where curiosity is encouraged, ideas are welcomed and you will have the opportunity to further develop your expertise in antenna design and electromagnetic simulation.What will be your role?During this internship, you will investigate and compare different phased-array antenna technologies suitable for E-band satellite communications. You will assess their expected performance and explore the main trade-offs related to efficiency, scanning range, complexity and practical implementation.Based on this analysis, you will select one or more promising concepts and design antenna elements that can operate efficiently while supporting a wide beam-scanning range. You will use electromagnetic software simulators (e.g. Ansys HFSS or CST studio suite) to model, simulate and optimize the proposed designs.The internship will include different phases, such as:Reviewing relevant antenna-array technologies and design approaches;Defining performance requirements and comparison criteria;Modelling and comparing suitable array concepts;Designing and optimizing wide-scanning antenna elements in CST;Evaluating parameters such as efficiency, impedance matching, radiation pattern and scanning performance;Documenting the results and presenting recommendations for further development.The exact focus of the assignment can be refined together based on your interests, background and the results obtained during the first stages of the internship.By the end of the internship, you will have developed practical experience in antenna-array design, electromagnetic simulation, technical decision-making and the communication of research results. Your findings will support the selection and development of antenna technologies for future satellite communication systems. This internship is in the framework of a project between TNO and Viasat.What we expect from youFor this internship, we are looking for a university student pursuing a M.Sc. degree with a background in electrical engineering, telecommunications, applied physics or a related discipline. It helps if you bring good communication skills, result driven attitude, and focused in problem solving, but we are happy to support you in developing areas you want to learn more about. postings.description: About this positionWithin the Department of Sustainable Process and Energy Systems, the gas processing team works on minimizing the carbon footprint of chemical and energy processes by capturing CO2 via solvent absorption and on its eventual further transformation into synthetic fuels. Our team focuses on the development and scaling-up of strategies to remove and purify CO2 coming from a wide range of industries, including but not limited to waste-to-energy plants, cement production facilities, and large container ships.
